table.title: [adversarial] Rowspan taller than its rows
table.html:
StepOwnerNotes
PlanAnaAll three steps share one change ticket. Approval from the security review board is required before any production access is granted, and every action must be logged in the audit trail with the ticket number, the operator's name and the exact commands executed.
BuildBen
ShipCai

understanding.purpose: Show the owners of three sequential steps alongside a note shared by all three.
understanding.reading: Readers scan down the steps and owners, then read the shared note as context for the whole sequence; its height spans all three rows.
groups: Step and Owner form the row-by-row identification pair.
Notes applies to all three steps and carries the long-form context.
keep_intact: Individual words in the shared note
may_wrap: The shared note can wrap naturally across lines; its merged cell can use the combined height of the three step rows.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Give Notes 9px more by bringing Step and Owner close to their minimum intact widths. This may reduce a line while retaining clear row labels and headers.

acceptable.name: r0A
acceptable.note: Give Step and Owner their minimum intact widths and devote the remaining space to the shared note.

acceptable.name: r0B
acceptable.note: Give the two identifying columns more breathing room while preserving a generous measure for the note.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Give Step and Owner a little more breathing room than r0A while preserving most of the width for the shared note. This tests whether a modest increase in header space improves the balance without materially increasing the note's height.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Give Notes a modest increase while preserving a little more breathing room around the step and owner labels.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Keep Owner at its minimum width for the header and give Step one extra pixel, testing a slightly different balance within the identification pair while retaining maximum space for the note.

bad.name: r0C
bad.note: Emphasize the step-and-owner pair with spacious columns, accepting a taller, more heavily wrapped shared note.
bad.why: Step and Owner receive much more room than their short entries need, leaving the shared note in a narrow, 16-line column. The resulting tall rows make the three steps harder to scan together.

rationale: The three short step and owner entries act as paired row labels, while the long note applies to all three rows. r2A gives the labels enough space and preserves a broad, readable measure for the shared note, with no broken words or wrapped headers. Its balanced allocation also keeps the three rows visible as a compact group.

general: Give space in proportion to content needs and the relationships readers must scan, rather than assigning equal column widths.
A cell spanning several rows should remain readable while the individual rows remain easy to distinguish.
specific: The note spans all three data rows and dominates the width requirement; Step and Owner contain only short labels.
The preferred range is approximate and assumes the widths continue to sum to at most 359px, with small adjustments shared among the other columns.

tradeoffs: r1A gives the two label columns slightly more breathing room, while r0A gives the note one more pixel; both retain the same overall height and line count as r2A. r0B is more spacious for labels but makes the note longer.
uncertain: The differences among r0A, r1A and the r2 variants are subtle, so a reasonable designer could prefer another of them. The stated ranges are approximate visual tolerances, not independently rendered breakpoints.

critique.good: The compact Step and Owner columns keep each identification pair together and give the shared note the most room. All names and words remain intact, and the note reads as context for all three steps.
critique.problems: The identification columns are tight, particularly around the Owner header; the tall rows also leave substantial empty space beneath each step and owner.
critique.cause: Widths of 56px and 69px leave only 35px and 48px for text, respectively. The 234px Notes column still needs ten lines, whose combined height determines the three row heights.

critique.good: Step and Owner have more breathing room, while the shared note remains legible and all words stay intact.
critique.problems: The wider identification columns add empty space to already tall rows, and the note wraps onto an extra line. The result is taller without improving the relationship between the steps and their shared context.
critique.cause: Increasing Step to 75px and Owner to 85px reduces Notes to 199px.

critique.good: The step and owner labels have ample space, and the merged note still clearly applies to all three rows.
critique.problems: The identification columns are disproportionately wide for their short labels, while the note becomes a narrow, fragmented block. The resulting tall rows make the sequence harder to scan.
critique.cause: Step and Owner consume 95px and 105px, leaving Notes only 159px and forcing it to 16 lines.

critique.good: The headers, step names, and owners remain intact. The shared note is clearly associated with all three steps, and its words wrap without splitting.
critique.problems: The note occupies the full height of the three rows, leaving substantial empty space beneath each short step and owner. The three equal, tall rows make the sequence feel sparse, although the note remains readable.
critique.cause: The 224px Notes column gives the text 203px of usable width, producing ten lines. The merged cell's height is distributed across the three rows. Step and Owner have enough width to remain intact, so their extra space cannot be used to reduce the height much without narrowing them.

critique.good: Step and Owner remain intact and form a clear pair. The shared note wraps by whole words and visibly spans all three steps.
critique.problems: The long note creates tall rows with substantial empty space beneath the step and owner labels.
critique.cause: The 233px Notes column is close to the maximum available; the note’s length determines the shared height. Owner has 1px more than its stated minimum.

critique.good: All headers, names and note words remain intact, and the three rows are easy to distinguish.
critique.problems: The narrower note changes its line breaks without reducing the table’s height; the identification columns have a little unused width.
critique.cause: Step and Owner use 58px and 72px, leaving Notes 229px.

critique.good: Step and Owner fit intact at their minimum widths, leaving 233px for the shared note. The headers are clear, and the merged cell communicates that the note applies to every step.
critique.problems: The note’s length still produces tall rows and empty space under the short labels.
critique.cause: At 233px, Notes occupies the maximum width available while preserving the stated minimum widths for Step and Owner. The remaining height follows from the note’s length and the three-row span.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: Step and Owner take up most of the width despite their short entries, leaving Notes as a narrow, heavily wrapped column and stretching the three rows.

r0B.why: The note has a comfortable reading width and the short entries remain intact, though Step and Owner still have more space than they need.

ref_auto.why: Compact Step and Owner columns leave generous room for the shared note. The entries remain intact, and the three steps are easy to scan.

r2A.why: The columns are well proportioned and the rows scan clearly, although the note wraps a little less naturally than in C and F.

r0C.why: Wide Step and Owner columns leave the shared note cramped, producing many short lines and excessive height in the step rows.

r0A.why: The short Step and Owner entries fit comfortably, while the note gets enough width to read smoothly. The three rows remain distinct and easy to compare.

raw.unsure: C and F appear nearly identical at this image scale; their small width differences are difficult to distinguish reliably.

r0B.why: The labels fit, but the narrow Notes column creates many short lines and leaves substantial empty space in the step and owner cells.

ref_equal.why: Notes is squeezed into very short lines, making the shared instruction difficult to read and stretching the three rows excessively.

r0A.why: Compact step and owner columns leave generous space for the long shared note. All labels fit, though the tall merged cell still creates noticeable empty space in the rows.

ref_auto.why: The compact label columns give the note room to read naturally, while keeping the three steps easy to distinguish. The merged note leaves some unavoidable empty row space.

r2A.why: The label columns fit their contents and the note has a readable measure, though it wraps a little more than in C and D.

r0C.why: Wide step and owner columns leave the note in a narrow strip, producing frequent line breaks and large empty areas beside it.

raw.unsure: C and D appear nearly identical at this image size; their small width differences do not produce a clear reading advantage.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
